bull.b: Sustained clinical improvements and reduced reliance on chronic immunotherapies strengthen miv-cel’s therapeutic differentiation in severe autoimmune disease. The favorable 12-month safety profile and planned rolling BLA create a durable pathway toward regulatory validation and potential commercialization.

Durable responses across stiff person syndrome and generalized myasthenia gravis support the broader applicability of Kyverna’s autoimmune CAR T approach. Replication across indications can improve development leverage, reinforce platform credibility, and expand future commercial opportunities.

A long-term manufacturing supply agreement addresses an important operational requirement for advancing a cell therapy toward approval and launch. Secured capacity can support clinical execution, improve preparation for commercialization, and reduce uncertainty around scaling miv-cel production.

bear.b: Kyverna has not yet demonstrated commercial revenue, leaving its business model dependent on clinical progress, regulatory approval, and future financing or partnering. Until a therapy is approved and launched, revenue visibility remains limited and operating costs are unlikely to be self-funded.

Deeply negative operating and free cash flow indicate substantial ongoing funding needs while Kyverna conducts development and clinical activities. Continued burn can require additional capital before product revenue begins, increasing financing dependence and potentially constraining development priorities.

The shrinking equity cushion reflects accumulated losses and reduces financial resilience as development spending continues. Although leverage remains relatively low, further losses may increase reliance on equity issuance or other financing, creating dilution risk and limiting strategic flexibility.
